title: London not ready for driverless 'robotaxis', report warns
key_facts: The London Assembly's transport committee urged Transport for London (TfL) to withhold approval for a full rollout of robotaxis until stronger safety measures are in place.

The committee said it had not heard sufficient evidence to persuade it that London should welcome autonomous passenger services; it was not convinced by safety claims from operators including Waymo, Wayve and Baidu.
Concerns named: passenger safety (assault, medical emergency, coercion with no driver), congestion, pollution, and TfL's lack of powers to cap vehicle numbers or revoke an operator's licence.

The report makes 13 recommendations, including tougher safety standards, more TfL control over permits, monitoring of congestion, accessibility for disabled people and support for workers whose jobs are at risk.
A YouGov survey cited in the report found 29 per cent of Londoners supported driverless vehicles and 42 per cent opposed.

The government and companies had planned fully driverless commercial taxis in London by spring 2026; TfL has not published its guidance, says it is 'not in a rush', and as of late 2026 no operator has finished the national (DVSA) approval process; a wider UK rollout now looks more likely in 2027.
quote_evidence: The London Assembly's transport committee has urged Transport for London (TfL) to withhold approval for a full rollout of so-called ‘robotaxis’ until stronger safety measures are in place.
A YouGov survey mentioned in the report found that just 29 per cent of Londoners supported introducing driverless vehicles, while 42 per cent were opposed.
As of late 2026, no operator has successfully completed the multi-stage approval process.
why_it_matters_hint: An official London body is telling the transport authority to hold back driverless taxis, which slows a rollout already behind its spring 2026 target.
